title: 12 V 5 W incandescent lamp on a base

sources.citation: UN ECE Regulation No. 37 (filament lamps for power-driven vehicles), category W5W: a 12 V wedge-base signal lamp whose 5 W is defined at R37's 13.5 V test voltage. Taking 5 W at 12 V (ratedPowerW at ratedVoltageV) is a game-design simplification. Only the rated values are used; the regulation's text and data sheets are not reproduced.

game-design inside published behaviour: small low-voltage vacuum signal lamps run their tungsten filaments at roughly 2500 to 2900 K (lamp makers' miniature-lamp catalogues give colour temperatures in that range; a household 100 W lamp runs nearer 2850 K). 2700 K is taken. With tungsten's resistivity (Jones and Langmuir, 1927) it gives the lamp a cold resistance of about 1/15 of its hot one, which is where the cold-start inrush comes from.

game-design inside published behaviour: a small signal lamp's filament heats and cools in tens of milliseconds, its inrush decaying over a few tens of milliseconds. 50 ms is taken as the small-signal thermal time constant at the rated point; with the 5 W rating it implies about 0.4 mJ/K of heat capacity, a filament of a couple of milligrams of tungsten.

Physics from H. A. Jones and I. Langmuir, General Electric Review 30 (1927): a filament's cold-to-hot resistance ratio is ρ(T_r)/ρ(T_a), 13.5 to 16.1 for rated temperatures of 2500 to 2900 K at a 293 K ambient. The source and lead resistance in series lower the current ratio, so the tested inrush band is 10 to 15 times the settled current.
game-design: the lamp stands in a holder on a 50 × 50 mm base, 60 mm tall, with a screw terminal on each side of the base; not modelled on a product.
